answer.answer:
The court shall be a rectangle marked out with lines 40 mm wide (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Law 1.1).
A shuttle landing on a line is 'in', not 'out': under Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Law 13.3.1, it is a fault only if the shuttle lands outside the boundaries of the court, i.e. not on or within the boundary lines. The line judge indicates whether the shuttle landed 'in' or 'out' on the line(s) assigned (Law 17.4), and, per Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.4, if the shuttle lands in the Line Judge says nothing but points to the line with the right hand while looking towards the Umpire.
For contrast, Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.3 requires the Line Judge to call 'Out' promptly with both arms extended horizontally when the shuttle lands out, no matter how far, and Clause 8.6 says not to call or signal until the shuttle has touched the floor or anything outside the court boundaries (except a player) — so a shuttle touching a boundary line is never called out.
